title: Equivalent Expressions
subtitle: Combine, Expand & Factor with Signs
bounds: T1-T4: every coefficient and constant in a prompt, in the correct answer and in every step between has size 1-12 (single-letter variables, one or two per item, no x^2 term); an outside multiplier has size 1-10 (a bare minus is -1) and each product is a times-table fact with a result of size <= 12; a combined coefficient or constant is never 0 and never over 12 in size. T4 GCF 2-6 (or its negative), the parts inside the bracket 1-6 with no common factor. T5 (PROTOCOL 4b): percents 10 20 25 30 40 50 60 75 off or down and 5 10 20 30 40 50 up; decimals at most 2 places and 2 non-zero digits; fractions proper, denominators 2-12 with lcm <= 12, results proper and in simplest form; perimeter: width w, length k times w plus c, with k 1-3 and c 1-6.

tiers.name: Combine Like Terms
tiers.description: Combine like terms when some coefficients are negative: 5x − 8x = −3x.

tiers.name: Distribute Negatives
tiers.description: Multiply a bracket by a negative number or a minus sign: −3(x − 4) = −3x + 12.

tiers.name: Factoring
tiers.description: Pull out a common factor, even a negative one: −4x + 8 = −4(x − 2).

tiers.name: Rewrite to Show Meaning
tiers.description: Same value, new form: 20% off p is 0.8p, and a + 0.05a is 1.05a.

WRONG_SIGN.student: Right size, wrong sign. Check which number is bigger and what its sign is.
WRONG_SIGN.teacher: Combines to the right size but writes the wrong sign on the variable term or the constant.

DROPPED_VARIABLE.student: Keep the letter. Only the coefficients combine; the letter stays on.
DROPPED_VARIABLE.teacher: Combines the numbers and drops the variable (or leaves it off a result that has one).

UNLIKE_COMBINED.student: Only like terms combine. A letter term and a plain number can't merge.
UNLIKE_COMBINED.teacher: Combines unlike terms (a variable term with a constant, or two different letters).

IGNORED_MINUS.student: A minus sign means take that term away. Don't turn it into a plus.
IGNORED_MINUS.teacher: Treats a subtracted term (or group) as if it were added.

NO_COEF_ONE.student: A letter alone is 1 of it (a is 1a, −a is −1a). Don't skip it.
NO_COEF_ONE.teacher: Skips a term whose coefficient 1 is not written.

ADD_SIZES.student: Different signs: subtract the sizes, keep the sign of the bigger one.
ADD_SIZES.teacher: Adds the sizes of two numbers with different signs instead of subtracting them.

DROPPED_TERM.student: Don't leave a term out. Every term is either combined or kept.
DROPPED_TERM.teacher: Leaves a term out of the result (a different letter, or the second like term).

PARTIAL_DIST.student: Multiply EVERY term inside ( ) by the outside number, not just the first.
PARTIAL_DIST.teacher: Applies the outside multiplier to the first term only.

SIGN_INSIDE.teacher: Gets the sign of a product wrong (negative times negative kept negative, or a sign flipped).

NEG_FIRST_ONLY.student: A minus in front of ( ) changes EVERY sign inside: −(2x + 5) = −2x − 5.
NEG_FIRST_ONLY.teacher: Applies a leading minus to the first term in the bracket only.

IGNORED_OUTER_MINUS.student: Keep the outside minus. −3(x − 4) means −3 times each term.
IGNORED_OUTER_MINUS.teacher: Distributes the size of a negative multiplier and drops its sign.

DROPPED_NEG.student: Don't lose a minus sign. It stays with the term it belongs to.
DROPPED_NEG.teacher: Drops the negative sign on one term (inside a bracket, a group or a factored form).

FIRST_TERM_ONLY.student: A minus in front of ( ) flips EVERY sign inside, not just the first.
FIRST_TERM_ONLY.teacher: Changes the sign of only the first term of the group being subtracted.

PARTIAL_FACTOR.student: Divide EVERY term by the factor you take out, not just the first.
PARTIAL_FACTOR.teacher: Factors the common factor out of one term only and leaves the other unchanged.

SIGN_FACTOR.student: Dividing by a negative flips the sign: −4x + 8 = −4(x − 2).
SIGN_FACTOR.teacher: Factors out a negative but keeps the old sign inside the bracket.

SUB_FOR_DIV.student: Factoring divides each term by the factor. Subtracting it is wrong.
SUB_FOR_DIV.teacher: Subtracts the common factor from each term instead of dividing.

ONE_TERM_FACTOR.student: Pull out what BOTH terms share, not just one term's number.
ONE_TERM_FACTOR.teacher: Factors out one term's number instead of the greatest common factor.

PART_ONLY.student: That's only the extra part. Combine it with the whole: 1 + 0.2 = 1.2.
PART_ONLY.teacher: Gives only the percent part (or the decimal part) and loses the whole amount.

PERCENT_AS_NUMBER.student: A percent is a part OF the amount (like 0.2p), not a plain 20 or 0.2.
PERCENT_AS_NUMBER.teacher: Adds or subtracts the percent as a plain number instead of taking that part of the amount.

WRONG_DIRECTION.student: Off or a drop means subtract (1 − 0.2). A rise or tax means add (1 + 0.2).
WRONG_DIRECTION.teacher: Adds where the situation subtracts, or subtracts where it adds.

PLACE_VALUE.student: Check the decimal point: 5% is 0.05 and 50% is 0.5.
PLACE_VALUE.teacher: Misplaces the decimal point converting between a percent and a decimal.

RATIO_AS_CHANGE.student: 1.2p is 120% of p. The change is only how far it is from 100%.
RATIO_AS_CHANGE.teacher: Reports the whole multiplier as the percent of change (1.2 as 120%).

ADD_ACROSS.student: Don't add the bottoms. Use a common denominator and add only the tops.
ADD_ACROSS.teacher: Adds (or subtracts) numerators and denominators straight across.

NO_CONVERT.student: Rename BOTH fractions with the common denominator, then add the tops.
NO_CONVERT.teacher: Uses the common denominator but combines the original numerators.

MULTIPLIED.student: Like terms ADD or SUBTRACT their coefficients. Don't multiply them.
MULTIPLIED.teacher: Multiplies the coefficients of like terms.

HALF_PERIMETER.student: The perimeter goes all the way around: two widths AND two lengths.
HALF_PERIMETER.teacher: Adds one width and one length, half the perimeter.

MISSING_SIDE.student: Count all 4 sides: the width twice and the length twice.
MISSING_SIDE.teacher: Counts the width once and the length twice (or the reverse).
